newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Nov. 4, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Oracle Corp and Microsoft Corp will both flesh out their initiatives for distributed computing this week, with Oracle hosting a user conference in San Francisco and Microsoft a developers' conference in Long Beach, Calif.
Oracle will discuss its Network Computing Architecture plans, PC Week reported, in its November 4 issue.

Long distance carriers such as AT&T and MCI Communications Corp are still not cleared to provide dial-up ISDN telephone service, despite slated plans from both companies to begin offering ISDN Internet services this past summer, PC Week reported Nov. 4. And for the most part, the regional bell operating companies are not able to provide the high speed digital phone service outside their regions. -----------

COMPUTERWORLD - Oracle Corp is set to unveil this week its own low-cost network computer device based on an Intel Corp Pentium chip and available in mid-1997, Computerworld reported November 4. A Java-based suite of applications containing a word processor, spreadsheet and other software will be ready in the first quarter of 1997.

Microsoft Corp chairman Bill Gates acknowledged that the latest version of Windows NT 4 will not work with some existing 16-bit Windows 95 applications and computer users won't get relief from the incompatability problem until the release of Windows NT 5.0 sometime in 1997, Computerworld also reported.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - U.S. Regional Bell telephone giants have stepped up their campaign to force Internet access providers to pay increased network charges to cover the costs of preventing the phone network from becoming overloaded and grinding to a halt, Communications Week reported in its November 4 issue. The assault on this cornerstone of U.S. Federal Communications Commission policy -- designed to encourage use of the Internet -- is designed to sway the FCC's decision-making on inteconnection rules allowing new entrants into local phone markets.

ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING TIMES - Broadcasters and the HDTV Grand Alliance partners are scheduled to meet with computer industry and film-industry executives Monday to work out a schedule for talks aimed at breaking the logjam over approval of the controversial digital television standard, EE Times reported in its November 4 issue.

Cadence Design Systems $420 million proposed acquisition of Cooper and Chyan Technology is the most expensive in the history of electronic design automation and will alter the competitive landscape in the PC-board and ICAD industries.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Dell Computer Corp has an alarmingly high "dead on arrival" rate of its PCs, compared with other major systems vendors, according to computer reseller executives, Computer Reseller News reported Nov. 4.

Oracle Corp will announce a new partnership with Netscape Communications Corp for developing Web-based applications, to be unveiled at Oracle's developer conference this week, CRN reported on November 4.

Hewlett-Packard Co and Intel Corp are planning to stretch out their existing microprocessor lines with one additional release before the introduction of Merced, their joint microprocessor architecture, CRN reported.

INFOWORLD - Companies negotiating long distance phone rates will need to become more saavy in the wake of a little known provision of the U.S. telecom reform act that frees long-distance carriers from requirements to publicly disclose tarrif information, Infoworld reported November 4.

Netscape Communications Corp is set to announce this week its plans to include Secure Computing Corp technology that allows corporate network administrators to control employee access to Web sites such as sports, sex, employment searching and entertainment.

INFORMATION WEEK - Microsoft Corp is releasing this week a preview version of an industrial-strength directory service to be built into the forthcoming version of Windows NT, while Novell Inc and Banyan Systems Inc are positioning their existing directory services across many product lines, Information Week reported Nov. 4.

Several executives in Xerox Corp's Information Systems organization have left the company in recent months, but the company said the exits have not created major problems, Information Week reported Nov. 4.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Intel Corp is developing a one-chip implementation of the PentiumPro processor called Klamath and a graphics accelerator, called Auburn, which will be its new PC platform and will put pressure on graphics chips makers, microprocessor developers and add-in card makers, EBN reported in the Nov. 4 issue.
The electronics industry kicked into high gear in October, as new orders and production reached their highest levels of the year, according to a poll by Electronic Buyers' News.

MACWEEK - Apple Computer Inc and Be were in negotiations last week, hashing out a deal that could bring Be's operating system into Apple's fold. Apple plans to merge the microkernel from the Mac OS 8, formerly known as Copland, with Be's BeOS application model. The company has reportedly set late summer 1997 as the earliest time from for delivery of the hybrid operating system, MacWeek reported on Nov. 4.
